assessment.overall_rationale: The strongest correspondences are the nearly identical tip-cell sprouting modules and the shared Kcnj2-centered mechanosensing modules, while the remaining similarities reflect narrower overlap in endothelial identity or TGF-β-dependent brain vascular biology.

pair_scores.rationale: Both modules describe the same Angpt2/Cxcr4/Cdc42ep3-positive tip-cell sprouting program, with matching Nrp1 promotion and Tek opposition in postnatal brain endothelium.
They share brain vascular patterning genes and angiogenic-versus-arterial identity features, but one centers on active tip-cell sprouting whereas the other centers on arteriovenous specification.
The modules share only the broad setting of specialized brain endothelium, with distinct angiogenic and BBB transport-mechanosensing outputs.

Both concern brain endothelial tip-cell angiogenesis, but the left module specifically requires TGF-β/ALK5 signaling for diving-tip identity while the right centers on Nrp1–CDC42 and Angpt2–Tek sprouting control.

Angpt2-linked nonarterial identity and postnatal brain vascular development overlap, but TGF-β-dependent diving-tip formation and arteriovenous specification are different central mechanisms and outputs.

Both assign a positive role to Tgfbr1/Tgfbr2 signaling in brain endothelial development, but one predicts diving-tip and deep-plexus defects while the other emphasizes BBB integrity alongside transport and mechanosensing.
Aside from their shared brain endothelial context, membrane ion-channel mechanosensing and angiogenic tip-cell sprouting have different mechanisms and validation phenotypes.
Rgs6 and neurovascular specialization provide peripheral overlap, but membrane calcium and flow sensing are mechanistically distinct from arteriovenous identity specification.

Both center partly on endothelial Kcnj2-mediated flow sensing, but the left extends this to calcium-channel microdomains whereas the right combines mechanosensing with BBB glutamate transport and TGF-β-dependent barrier integrity.
